subject: Physics
title: Diffraction and Interference
learningOutcomes: Describe the interference of waves, coherent sources and the conditions for constructive and destructive interference.
Explain Young's double-slit experiment and derive the path difference \(d\sin\theta\) and fringe spacing \(\Delta y=\lambda L/d\).
Describe interference of water, sound, light and microwaves in two-source set-ups.
Explain diffraction and use \(a\sin\theta=m\lambda\) for a single slit.
Describe a diffraction grating and use \(d\sin\theta=m\lambda\) with \(d=1/N\).
Explain the wave-particle behaviour of electrons in the double-slit experiment and the Copenhagen and Many-Worlds interpretations.

sections.heading: Interference of Waves
sections.body: Interference is the superposition of two or more waves in the same medium. Where the waves arrive in phase they add up (constructive interference, path difference \(m\lambda\)); where they arrive out of phase they cancel (destructive interference, path difference \((m+\tfrac12)\lambda\)). A steady pattern needs coherent sources — same frequency and constant phase difference.

sections.heading: Young's Double-Slit Experiment
sections.body: In 1801 Thomas Young passed light through two narrow slits a distance d apart and saw alternate bright and dark fringes on a screen a distance L away. The path difference at angle θ is \(d\sin\theta\). Bright fringes: \(d\sin\theta=m\lambda\); dark fringes: \(d\sin\theta=(m+\tfrac12)\lambda\). The fringe positions are \(y=m\lambda L/d\) and the spacing is \(\Delta y=\lambda L/d\).

sections.heading: Interference of Different Waves
sections.body: Interference is shown by water waves in a ripple tank (two dippers), by sound from two loudspeakers driven by one oscillator, by light from two slits, and by microwaves from two slits in a metal sheet. All of these need coherent sources.

sections.heading: Diffraction
sections.body: Diffraction is the spreading of waves around obstacles or through openings. It is greatest when the opening is about the size of the wavelength. For a single slit of width a the minima satisfy \(a\sin\theta=m\lambda\); the central maximum is wide and bright.

sections.heading: Diffraction Grating
sections.body: A grating has a very large number of equally spaced slits. If N is the number of lines per unit length, the grating element is \(d=1/N\). Maxima occur at \(d\sin\theta=m\lambda\); the bright lines are sharp and bright. Gratings are used in spectroscopy and appear as the rainbow colours on a CD.

sections.heading: Electrons and Interpretations
sections.body: Electrons fired one at a time at a double slit build up an interference pattern, showing wave-particle duality. The Copenhagen interpretation says a particle has no definite position until measured; the Many-Worlds interpretation says every possible outcome occurs in a separate branch of the universe.

definitions.definition: The superposition of two or more waves in the same medium, producing a larger or smaller resultant displacement.
Sources that emit waves of the same frequency with a constant phase difference.
The difference in the distances travelled by two waves to reach the same point; \(d\sin\theta\) for two slits.
Interference in which waves arrive in phase and the resultant amplitude is larger; path difference \(m\lambda\).
Interference in which waves arrive out of phase and the resultant amplitude is smaller; path difference \((m+\tfrac12)\lambda\).
The bending and spreading of waves around the edges of an obstacle or opening.
The distance between two consecutive bright (or dark) fringes, \(\Delta y=\lambda L/d\).
A surface with a large number of equally spaced slits (or grooves) that disperses light into spectra.
The distance d between two adjacent slits of a grating, \(d=1/N\).

examTips: Write the path difference as \(d\sin\theta\) first — bright fringes need \(m\lambda\), dark fringes need \((m+\tfrac12)\lambda\); in this book the first dark fringe is m = 0.
Fringe spacing \(\Delta y=\lambda L/d\): convert nm, µm and mm to metres before substituting, and check the units of your answer.
For a grating, find d = 1/N first; the highest order is the largest whole number m with \(m\lambda/d<1\).

practiceQuestions.explanation: Interference is the superposition of two or more waves, giving a larger or smaller resultant displacement.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Two sources are coherent when they:

options: Have a constant phase difference and the same frequency

practiceQuestions.explanation: Coherent sources keep a constant phase difference (and the same frequency), so a stable interference pattern forms.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Constructive interference occurs when the path difference is:
practiceQuestions.explanation: A path difference of a whole number of wavelengths, \(m\lambda\), puts the waves in phase.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The fringe spacing in Young's double-slit experiment is:
If the screen distance L is doubled in a double-slit experiment, the fringe spacing:
practiceQuestions.explanation: \(\Delta y\propto L\), so doubling L doubles the fringe spacing.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Light of wavelength 600 nm falls on slits 0.5 mm apart; the screen is 2 m away. The fringe spacing is:
A diffraction grating with N lines per unit length has grating element:
A grating has 500 lines per mm. Its grating element is:
Diffraction is most noticeable when the slit width is:

options: Much larger than the screen distance

practiceQuestions.explanation: Waves spread out most when the opening is about the size of the wavelength.

practiceQuestions.prompt: In the Copenhagen interpretation, a particle:

options: Has a definite path at all times
Has no definite position until it is measured
Splits the universe at each measurement

practiceQuestions.explanation: Copenhagen: the wave function describes probabilities; the position becomes definite on measurement.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Interference is observed only for sound waves.
practiceQuestions.explanation: False — water, sound, light, microwaves and even electrons show interference.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Using light of longer wavelength increases the fringe spacing in a double-slit experiment.
practiceQuestions.explanation: True — \(\Delta y=\lambda L/d\) is proportional to λ.

practiceQuestions.prompt: When the waves arrive in phase and add up, the interference is called ______.
The bending and spreading of waves around the edges of an obstacle or opening is called ______.
For slits d apart, the path difference at angle θ is d ______ θ.

sequencingActivity.prompt: Arrange these fringes in order of increasing distance from the centre of the screen.
sequencingActivity.explanation: Positions are 0, ½Δy, Δy, 1½Δy, 2Δy — maxima at mΔy and minima at (m + ½)Δy.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: In a double-slit experiment with 500 nm light, d = 0.2 mm and L = 1.6 m, what is the distance of the 3rd bright fringe from the central maximum?
A grating of element 2.5 µm is used with 500 nm light. What is the highest order of maximum that can be seen?
bossBattleQuestions.explanation: \(m\lambda/d=\sin\theta\le1\) so \(m\le d/\lambda=5\); but at m = 5, \(\sin\theta=1\) (θ = 90°) the maximum is not observed, so the highest visible order is 4.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A grating has 400 lines per mm. At what angle is the first-order maximum for 600 nm light? (\(\sin\theta=0.24\))
Two waves of wavelength 400 nm reach a point with a path difference of 1000 nm. What is observed?

options: Neither, the waves do not overlap

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: 1000/400 = 2.5, an odd multiple of ½, so destructive interference — a dark fringe.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Electrons fired one at a time at a double slit still build up an interference pattern. What does this show?

options: Each electron behaves as a wave and interferes with itself

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: The pattern appears even with single electrons, showing wave-particle duality — each electron interferes with itself.
